In this species the surfaces of the cells are lightly striated, giving the t�allus a rather
yellowish-green look that is surprisingly easy to recognise once it is known. However,
greener forms are not unusual and can be very confusing. The apices of the branches
are rather blunt. It is reasonably common on soil or rotting wood in wet forest and
rainfores!, and only R. colensoi is similar.

R. eriocaula                                                                         TV
This is a mainly Tasmanian species with a more or less dendroid habit. The shoots are
up to 35 mm tall and consist of a stem and a semicircular, flattened frond. The thallus
i_ s papillose, making it appear rather rough or bristly under a hand lens. The branches
are tripinnately branched. This species seems to be confined to very wet rainforest.

1<: watt5ianaa                                                                    WTVAN
This is a common species of wet forest and rainforest in Tasmania, but it is quite
rare on the mainland. It is usually very densely branched, with two types of
branches. The primary branches are usually prostrate, 2 to 3 mm wide, and often
hidden by the secondary branches, which are only 0.5 mm or so wide and rather
palmate. The apices of the terminal branches are dissected, but this is often
impossible to see with a hand lens.

 Mosses & Allied Plants of Southern Australia


Riccia Ricciaceae
Intermittently wet soil in drier regions is the typical habitat of most species in this
genus. Some grow in wet envjronments, and a few are aquatic. The thallus is branched
once or twice, so that plants can form small rosettes with the branches appearing to
radiate outwards. There is usually a conspicuous sunken, longitudinal furrow, especially
near the apex of each branch. The upper surface of the thallus can have either a smooth,
uniform appearance with regularly spaced air-holes (subgenus Riccia), or a rough
surface with a honeycombof irregular holes which often become enlarged with age
(subgenus Ricciella). The ventral surface of the thallus generally carries scales, whose
nµmber, size and v{sibility are useful diagnostic features for some species. The
sporophyte consists of what Scott (1985) called a 'bag of spores' within the thallus.

Similar species: Asterella spp., Enigmella thallina, Plagiochasma rupestre, Reboulia
gueenslandica, Targionia hypophylla

Subgenus Riccia

Richardia scabra, commonly called rough Mexican clover or Florida pusley, is a species of flowering plant in the family Rubiaceae. It is widespread, native to warm areas of both North America, South America and East African countries like in Central Kenya.
